✦ STRATEGIC DILEMMAS ✦
The Five Questions Every Analytics Leader Must Answer

Most analytics initiatives fail not from mathematical error, but from strategic disconnection. This curriculum maps the journey to resolution.

01
How do we build an authentic data culture?

Moving beyond HIPPO (Highest Paid Person's Opinion) to hypothesis-driven experimentation, just as Capital One reinvented retail banking.

EXPLORE STRATEGIC RESOLUTION
02
What should our analysts actually work on?

Protecting top quantitative talent from low-value ad-hoc spreadsheet requests by ruthlessly focusing on the "Big Rocks": Revenue, Cost, and Risk.

EXPLORE STRATEGIC RESOLUTION
03
What does the first 90 days look like?

The structured 4-phase playbook: listening in month one, executing an undeniable quick win in month two, and scaling enterprise governance in month three.

EXPLORE STRATEGIC RESOLUTION
04
How do we align 48 stakeholders around an uncomfortable answer?

The San Jose International Airport case: reducing a $4.5B capital expansion to $1.5B by co-designing simulation assumptions with airlines, city planners, and federal agencies.

EXPLORE STRATEGIC RESOLUTION
05
Where will we stumble along the way?

An unvarnished catalog of 36 failure modes across Executive Sponsors, Analytics Managers, Business Partners, and Analysts.

EXPLORE STRATEGIC RESOLUTION
✦ THE RIVER OF INSIGHTS JOURNEY ✦
Explore the Five Lands

Each region along the river reflects the temperament and demands of a specific leadership stage.

CHAPTER 7
Peach Village
Analytics and Leadership

"Where the river remembers spring: vision, culture, and foundations."

Analytics leadership is not about mastering mathematical models; it is about building the culture, literacy, and decision-making framework where data informs every significant strategic bet.

SAIL IN 3D
CHAPTER 8
Bamboo Forest
Competing on Analytics

"Navigating the dense canopy: choosing what to do and who does it."

Winning companies focus their scarce analytical talent on the "Big Rocks"—the high-stakes levers that move the profit needle—while establishing the right organizational structure to sustain momentum.

SAIL IN 3D
CHAPTER 9
Mountain Valley
The Analytics Leader's 90-Day Playbook

"The timed climb: 30 days to assess, 60 days to execute and scale."

A structured, battle-tested roadmap for any incoming analytics leader to establish credibility, secure executive trust, deliver immediate value, and lay the foundation for long-term scalability.

SAIL IN 3D
CHAPTER 10
Lantern Bridge
Making It Happen

"Bridging the divide: aligning 48 stakeholders and driving real execution."

The definitive playbook on stakeholder alignment, navigating organizational politics, and turning complex quantitative insights into consensual executive decisions.

SAIL IN 3D
CHAPTER 11
Forgotten Garden
Common Pitfalls

"Among the ancient ruins: 36 traps across four organizational roles."

A candid, cautionary exploration of the recurring pitfalls that derail analytics initiatives across Executives, Analytics Managers, Business Partners, and Data Analysts.

SAIL IN 3D
THE HARBOUR
Final Stop
Case Studies Archive

"Where the river meets the open sea."

Six landmark enterprise case studies: Capital One, Netflix, Google, Booking.com, Uber, and San Jose Airport.

Capital One: How Data-Driven Testing Revolutionized Consumer Credit
THE STRATEGIC CHALLENGE

In the late 1980s, credit card issuers relied on homogenous terms and subjective human underwriting, leading to high default rates and underserved credit segments.

WHAT HAPPENED

Co-founders Richard Fairbank and Nigel Morris engineered the Information-Based Strategy (IBS). Every piece of customer interaction was structured as a controlled micro-experiment—testing card limits, teaser interest rates, fee structures, and rewards.

EXPLORE MEASURED OUTCOME & METRICS
THE KEY LESSON

"Analytics is not an IT cost center; it can be the entire engine of corporate strategy and competitive differentiation."

SEE ALL 6 CASES
+67% CapEx Saved
$3B
San Jose Airport Cost Optimization

Capital expansion budget successfully reduced from $4.5B to $1.5B via transparent simulation modeling across 48 stakeholders while maintaining 100% required passenger throughput.

“
"We structured thousands of micro-tests. If you make experimentation the foundational business model, market disruption follows naturally."
— RICHARD FAIRBANK, FOUNDER OF CAPITAL ONE
